strongest_angle: Workplace financial education programs provide a more reliable foundation for long-term financial confidence and positive behavioral change than higher income alone, according to the new Voya Financial Confidence Index.

key_facts.fact: The America’s Financial Confidence Index from Voya Financial, Inc. identifies a significant gap between how U.S. workers feel about their finances and their actual daily financial habits.

Research from the Employee Benefit Research Institute (EBRI) indicates that employees who engage in employer-provided financial education report higher levels of literacy, satisfaction, and confidence.
A study by the FINRA Foundation found that over 50 percent of participants in workplace-based financial education programs had household incomes exceeding 150,000 dollars.
Employee Benefit News reports a 21-point disparity separating worker confidence in retirement planning from other critical financial expectations.
